name: Umbra Collective Sensor-Blind Cap
description:
A baseball-style cap with an IR LED array embedded in the brim that floods facial-recognition cameras with invisible light, rendering the wearer's face unreadable to automated systems. To human eyes, the cap looks completely normal. To cameras, the wearer's face is a white-out blur.

Sold openly in Shelf markets as a 'privacy accessory' and quietly tolerated by most security forces who consider it a nuisance rather than a threat. Higher-tier zones with military-grade surveillance systems can compensate for the IR flooding, limiting the cap's effectiveness to mid- and lower-tier districts.
functionality: IR camera blinding, facial recognition defeat (effective against civilian-grade systems)
what_it_says: You paid Φ90 to become invisible to every cheap camera on the street. Best investment you ever made.
story_hooks: A politician is photographed buying Sensor-Blind Caps in bulk — raising questions about who they're distributing them to and why they want those people invisible.
